speaker: Doctor

The normal lab results make a drug-induced lupus or SLE less likely, as they typically show cytopenias or elevated inflammatory markers. Given the blistering on your forearm, painful oral ulcers, and genital pain, could you describe exactly how the skin lesions look (e.g., are they tense, flaccid, or crusted) and have you noticed any new sun-sensitive rashes on your face or arms?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your hiking history and the specific symptoms of blisters on your forearm and painful mucosal ulcers, I need to rule out an infectious cause. Did you have any recent contact with ticks, deer, or rabbits while hiking? Also, have you noticed any flu-like symptoms such as fever, chills, or swollen lymph nodes in your neck?

REQUEST TEST: RPR, VDRL, and T. pallidum particle agglutination assay (TP-PA).
REQUEST IMAGES: Full-body skin exam and oral mucosa.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I am concerned about Syphilis given your hiking history and the combination of genital pain, painful oral ulcers, and a blistering skin lesion. Have you noticed any painless sores (chancres) at the genital site in the past, and can you describe the current forearm lesion as a single large blister or multiple smaller vesicles?

REQUEST TEST: RPR, VDRL, and T. pallidum particle agglutination assay (TP-PA).
REQUEST IMAGES: Full-body skin exam and oral mucosa.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda (PCT)

I have ruled out drug-induced lupus, SLE, and Syphilis due to your normal lab results and lack of specific secondary signs. The combination of blisters on sun-exposed skin (forearm), painful oral/genital ulcers, and your history of hiking (potential iron exposure) strongly suggests an acute porphyria. Did you experience any darkening of your urine or abdominal pain? Please confirm if you have a family history of liver disease or hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Urine porphobilinogen (PBG) and uroporphyrin levels.
